Liberty is gaining, once again, the control that you rightly deserve as an individual. Collective utopias are born from collaboration in the hands of independent agents. Cynicism against being a utopian is born from a cynicism over whether or not you have control.

How do we conceive of utopias as something attainable, when so many are under the impression that we do not have control? If it's emblematic of the present era that the futures in which we are trained are outside of our control, what better way to cope with this reality than to view hope with cynicism, and continue to believe that we indeed do not have control?

This is why systems that enable the greatest individual sovereignty precourse utopias. As it stands, we no longer feel in control of the future, and instead hope that some displaced outside hero will resolve over our present to lead us from dystopia in a hero’s journey. The truth is far more urgent, and far more in the hands of those who read this.

The power of one's own agency roots itself in immovable earth against a lack of control - the willingness to remain immobile against the flows that surround us is a protest against cynicism and giving up hope. If this is true, the agency of hopeful collectives enable even greater control over collective fate. We can then measure attainment of the much grander, more expansive utopias that agency-based optimism offers us.

We deserve utopias, but we specifically deserve several. We deserve a hopeful version of the future that is under our control, where we harness collective agency to achieve what seems under our present cynicism to be impossible. It is only impossible if we believe that reaching utopias is outside of our control.

The greatest problems of our age are borne out of giving up control to others, and some of our greatest achievements have been in favor of this control being defeated and sovereignty - liberty - returned to individuals and collectives. Climate change is a coordination problem, but it is also a problem of control - we do not believe that it is something on which we can exert control. We believe that there are other forces at play that determine the outcome. If this is true - indeed we are dystopia bound, but I do not believe that the human capacity for agency can be so easily defeated. Instead, it must be nurtured.

An agency for collectives to build away from dystopias and toward utopias requires that they, too, have agency, both in the futures that they experience and the missions that they take on with others. Technologies that enable agency are therefore imperative - because the tools of agency are what inspire an individual with the truth that they do indeed have control. Tools that we do not need to trust to control us, even more so - because tools in whose operation we have no doubt of subterfuge over our agency cannot take control from us.

We do not possess many tools that do not manipulate us in turn - we have not made many of them with intention. In the progress of human society, we must see carefully what great agency can be offered to individuals by our tools as well as the potential in these tools for robbing control that may lie in wait from their use. Oftentimes we can't predict these faults, but ownership over our mistakes is equally pressing - if we are inspired (as collectives and as individuals) to believe that we have a hand in the mistakes of humanity, we can atone for them, even learn and grow from them. To believe that there is no ownership over collective fault is dire at best, so it is imperative that we are inspired with a culture of ownership that documents and hardens ownership over our faults. If we maintain that we do not have a hand in our own mistakes, we can never seek to improve from them, and then all arguments to do so seem baseless.

It may be that the greatest human achievement is to seek means through which individuals feel collective utopias are attainable - and that these utopias are born from human intention, from the hands of individuals and collectives, and in the interest of all those that utopias must serve. Great hope unfolds from the belief that potential is an achievement at the hand of collectives, and utopias can only be achieved if great hope is afforded as a function of working toward utopias; people must be enabled to believe that utopias are possible because they themselves are capable of creating them.

item.title: Orbweaver
item.description:
It was about ten feet long, mottled grey, and had the same texture as granite. I think if I hadn't known about stone already, I'd have uncovered it and wouldn't have known that it didn't belong there, but a 4-year degree in geology leading to a masters in schist incursions told me otherwise. Besides, it didn't really feel like granite. There was something about it that felt at once less dense, but far heavier - as though it had the weight of an object, not a part of the landscape.

There was also something about it that told me I shouldn't tell anyone I'd found it. On the surface of it, sure, it was probably a little weird that a geology professor from a local college was spending their weekends digging pilot cores in the a neighborhood state park - but something told me that it was more than this. It wasn't until I uncovered it that it really clicked - I'd spent a week carefully peeling back the layers to reveal whatever had broken the tip of my spiral bore - but this realization had me settled in knowing that whatever this was was more than just a curiosity.

When I first figured out its total size, I didn't know what to do. I didn't have the skills to understand what to do next, so I took a ridiculous number of photographs. Somehow I was motivated to take these on film rather than digitally, as though taking pains to make sure that there wasn't a trace that I'd found this thing in the woods. This was echoed by how I covered the object back up, building a lattice of branches and covering it in dead leaves. I wasn't too worried someone would stumble on what I'd found, it was in a strange spot and at best, maybe a dog would run over to the area and piss on it.

When I developed the photos in my darkroom, things started to feel a bit more ominous. The images showed something completely different from what I'd photographed. In place of quiet-looking stone, there was a sleek, ornate, organic shape that approximated a minimal surface egg, a mathematical object that I'd remembered from the Topology courses I took alongside my master's program. It was a gunmetal gray, swiss-cheesed with paths through the object, and there was no way that this had developed naturally - the filigree-like pathways through the object made it appear symmetrical, all the more organic. There was no way this was a rock.

Also, the photographs had the object standing up.

When the first photos developed, this was the part that struck me with the most dissonance. The photographs looked as though I'd taken them of the object while it was standing on this end, several steps back in order to capture the entirety of the shape in frame. Worse yet, I couldn't shake the feeling that it was looking at me through the image - the same feeling a person has when they look back on a portrait of a friend looking directly into the frame - but I couldn't discern where the eyes might be. The whole thing seemed as though it was staring into the lens.

It was about 8pm when I developed the first images - just the time that the state park closed. After I'd gotten over the chill feeling of not knowing that sat in the forefront of my chest, so similar to a feeling of devastation, I packed a flashlight, a strobe, and my jacket, hopping back into my car to drive back toward the object. I ended up having to park in the middle school parking lot, toward the back, hoping that the car seemed inconspicuous, knowing that it probably wasn't - but when I drove into the lot there were no police patrolling the area, so I tried my luck. I was lucky that my training had me noting down the lat/long coordinates of my pet neighborhood incursion studies, having logged the location of the dig into a fitness watch, but I hadn't taken this approach to the site, and it was dark, and it was late November. There would be some bushwhacking involved.

I walked about a hundred feet into the woods guided by the watch, careful to let my eyes adjust, before I flipped on my flashlight in bug-proof mode and bathed the forest in front of me in red light. It clicked for me that I was doing something unusual - but the power that intrigue had over me was substantial. I was compelled, methodically stepping over the macabre shadows of logs and pushing aside bushes and branches, following the dim arrow on the LED surface of my watch with its proximity decreasing.

I watched the distance tick to zero, my mind finally growing accustomed to a recognition of my surroundings in a different light, and sure enough - the lattice of sticks and leaves were still over laying across my dig site. I reached into the loam I'd piled up in a corner of the site to pull out a rake I'd brought with me several digs before and began to clear away the cover I'd built. The object definitely wasn't standing. I took the photographs out of the backpack I'd brought with me, flipping the flashlight to natural glow, and again, the image of the object standing erect in the woods, light passing through the gaps, stared back at me from the photograph.

I decided to risk taking more photographs. I realized before I thought about doing so that I'd fully uncovered the object again, and before pulling out my camera, I shone my flashlight over the surface of the object. It looked no different than it had before, a granite-like texture that I couldn't place.

I set up my strobe - stepping back from the pit I'd dug up and positioned myself to take the image. Nothing was different. I looked around the woods, hoping nothing was looking back at me, but curiosity and a little bit of fear goaded me onward. It was not probable anyone would see the strobe go off unless they were in the woods with me. That was a chance I'd have to take.

I armed the strobe and the remote transmitter, stepped back, setting my focus at the distance I knew I was from the object, and depressed the shutter. One technique that I'd learned from shooting was to keep both eyes open when aiming, so that an object's framing in the final image matches what you see. The strobes went off.

For a split second, I knew I saw something other than what I'd been aiming at. The strobed image on my retina was of the object, on its end, lit against the night sky, long, tendrilled shadows passing through the objects holes. It wasn't what I'd come into the woods to find. Fuck. There was no way that just happened.

I stepped over to the dig pit, and the object clearly hadn't moved. Fear started creeping into my chest, but I stepped back to take another photograph. It didn't make any sense. I was aiming downward, but the image on my retina was looking upward, at the object against the canopy; not the image I was about to take again.

I held my breath, finger slowly pushing down the shutter. The strobe fired, and again, stark against my retinas was the object, staring back at me from a frame of the canopy against stars. There's no way this is happening.

I didn't know what to do. I lowered the camera and looked at the object, still lying in situ. It hadn't moved, there was no way that it had moved. I hesitated, breath tight in my chest. Looked down at my watch.

It was 3am. I'd been in the woods for 9 hours. There's no way this is happening.

I packed up my things. Something told me to cover the object back up, but I was terrified. Something was happening, here, something I didn't have words for, and that I knew no one would understand if I explained to them - it could only be if I showed them. When the object was covered back up, I stood back, looking at my dig site again. Fuck. I turned and began walking back, and immediately realized I hadn't logged the location of the parking lot or my track through the woods. FUCK.

Calm down. I pulled out my phone, pulled open my maps application. I wasn't far, I just had to head in the general direction of the lot. Thank goodness for technology. Fuck.

40 minutes slogged by. I didn't recognize anything I'd walked over getting to the site. Nothing looks the same in reverse. I kept checking my phone, every twenty feet or so, inching closer to the lot. Fuck. Terror was building in me. What the fuck did I just find?

At the edge of the lot, I saw my car, cloistered toward the edge of the lot. No police in the lot. Good. I walked toward my car, opened up the trunk, put down my things, opened the driver's side door, sat down. What the fuck did I just find? Turned on the car engine. What the fuck did I just find?

item.title: Caught in a loop
item.description:
I'm frustrated, I guess - for the most part, I feel as though I don't know what comes next for me anymore, and I'm really trying to figure that out in all the ways that I can- but I feel as though I'm caught in a loop and I don't know what it meant to come next like it's not clear to me. The dreams aren't coming anymore.
It's not as though I feel there's anything I can do about it, either. The world is shit. Most of our human experience is shit. I don't know what there is to look forward to and I can't really tell how it is that we're meant to dig our way out of it in any way other than to go through it, but the other side seems really dreary, and frustrating because I truly can't tell what you are meant to do when you get to the other side of that effort. Like, what are the dreams that people are meant to have after all of this? Are we supposed to feel as though there's any hope for a brighter future? It baffles me. I don't know how people can aspire to anything anymore. No amount of money is somehow going to make the rest of it come together and I'm watching other people put in the effort to create a life that I'm not sure I'll ever get to have. I'm 33 years old and I don't think that I have any dreams, there's this itching feeling that I'm meant to teach people, but I really can't tell if it's something that will ever happen for me because all I seem to be able to do so far is work. I'm tired, I want rest because I don't know what the other side of these feelings are. I can't see what I'm meant to do anymore, I don't really know what I'm going to do for others or the ways that I'll be able to do so because all of it is locked up against the barrier of having to think about how to make money. I'm tired of having to work like this, I'm tired of the idea that what I'm doing is something that actually means something to society when society is such bullshit, when so much of what we're dealing with is a continuous state of fear and rampage around the oppression of others. Maybe I'm just supposed to unplug, maybe I'm meant to feel disengaged.
That's probably where I'm going to end up - being disengaged feels as though it puts me in a place where I can actually think about a future without feeling as though I have to solve every problem in my present; they simply aren't my problems anymore. The other thing that comes to mind is discipline, it's the ability to get back into the mindset that I've had in the past that has yielded the results I wanted, where I was able to tell myself that there was more to my thoughts, where I was able to aspire to things. At some point, I stopped thinking like that, and I think it's because this world encourages to to feel hopeless. I'm aware of the fact that it's something I need to be responsible for, and as a result is something that I can do something about - it's just that in all the effort that I've had to make in my life to get through the experiences I've had and to become the person that I am, I'm not completely certain that I've wrapped my head around what comes next.

We knew this would happen though.

Yeah?

Yeah. This was the point of taking on your transition, and this is the thing that you knew was going to happen - that you'd get to the other side of this, that society would see you for who you are, but that because of this, you wouldn't know what to do next. That's ok - that's to be expected, and I think you know that by now.

Yeah, but I really didn't think I'd feel like this. I feel like this pretty often, this sense of foreboding that doesn't want to go away because I don't know what to do with my life.

You've already done a hell of a lot more than other people do. I hope you realize that; I know that sometimes, you do - but the reality is that escaping the human condition is something that people have always wanted to do. Remember that we wanted to build a church, that there is something to be found in telling people the Truth.

But what is the Truth? Am I forgetting to ask that question? I feel like I have been - like, all the thinking that I put into my subject matter area thinking, how much I know about networks, all of that-

It's not enough. You know that it's not enough, and I know that you're aware of this - that the work that you've put in is insubstantial compared to what needs to happen in order to get to where you want to. So you're 33. It's ok to disappear for a while as you work to figure yourself out. That's unsurprising to me, and it feels as though it's something that you're afraid of doing because you don't want to loose what you have. You don't have all that much, and what is actually yours will stay yours. I'm sure that you know that by now.

So how am I supposed to get to a place where I feel as though I'm actually making progress? I don't even know what that progress looks like anymore, because I don't know where I'm headed.

Remember the Hagakure.- the bravest of samurai charges forward toward death with no regard for his own life. That's how you can live your life, by being diligent, by being disciplined. This is the part that you haven't done yet, worked out how to get yourself to take on the hard work that you have always struggled with in order to become the person that you want to be.

But who do I want to be?

*I feel as though you experience glimmers of it on a constant basis - cool, collected, self-aware, confident, critical, kind, and around all of this, willing to go the distance needed to achieve things while making sure that you are taking care of yourself. Developing these abilities requires that you define it and stick to it, and I know that you've done the work to develop a kindness with yourself - so celebrate this part.

It's hard though - I feel as though as things are I am not really giving back to myself.

Have you asked yourself what it is that you want that would even feel like giving back to yourself?

No - not really, I guess.

Figure that out. You just ran a marathon at a blistering pace. You can probably do anything, so far as I've known you to do so.

Yeah but - I don't know what I need or want in order to get there.

~ chuckling ~ Yeah - that's sort of the point of my line of questioning. I don't think you know how to give back to yourself yet. Take a fucking vacation already, or do something like that - I don't know. Ask yourself what would mean something to you, and work toward that. Ask yourself what you wish that someone would do for you, and do that for yourself. It will go along way.

I guess I don't know what I actually want.

Well, for one, get laid. It feels like that's been on your list for a while and hasn't happened. Inma doesn't seem like it's high on her priorities, but you know it's on yours. You know what kind of energy you are looking for there.

Yeah.

So like I said - take care of yourself, give yourself what you're looking for. I can tell that you need it and that you're not getting it.

Ok.

Do I still want to get my doctorate? It feels as though I do, I'm pretty sure that I do.

What are the reasons that I want to? Is it because I want to have the doctorate, or is it because I want to learn something that I don't think I can learn anywhere else? Is that even possible? Is that something that I can count on, or will it be more of the same, will I get sucked into more organizational politics that will make it impossible for me actually to get what I want out of the situation?

item.title: Starting over
item.description:
There's nothing wrong with starting over, I tell myself, knowing that it isn't true and that at best I'm going to have to work through the details of a negative experience. There's nothing wrong with waking up in a different city, thinking mostly about the past and not really conspiring about the future.

There's an electricity in the air regardless - that part of the idea is trying to move an idea forward so that as much of everything can be implicated from the silence that surrounds it, and that there isn't much that can be done from questioning value on the way to getting there. It's cold in Paris, my fingers are having a hard time putting the letters into motion, I miss my dog.

Even the while, knowing that there is direction given to what it means to proceed and expecting that there will be even more in motion, we listen to the silence as though it's telling us something, as though the next step of construction will come from something other than popularization of a few concepts and phrases, rather than any sort of expectation that there's something to be done anout the reality that surrounds us. II'm not sure what the expetation is, but we'll have to pretend that we're going to get there when we get there. I'm not sure sure that's how things work.

If it does, then there's a lot for people to think about in the means of getting to wherever they expect that they will go. Too much language, too little anger about the state of things, too little adaptation. If the movement is neutral, then there will be no passion.

So what is the language to be used around expectation? What is the means through which solutions can be landed upon? How do you explain the route that must be taken, how do you land in a place that makes sense of the present, how do you overrule the silence of the unknown.

The reason that these things, in motion, require a heedlessness, is an attention toward recognizing that it must be done without thinking. It must be done without expecting that there's a sense to it all, and it must be done without expecting that the solution can and will be made from moving onward. Half of the work that needs to be done, at the least. Half of the expectation. Half of the assumption, half of the action. And what good would that do? How do you arrive in a place that makes sense of an expectation and meets it with a sequence of meanings and actions that do not know how to arrive in this place? The best things were made without planning for them, and because of this must be achieved without expecting that they will be made. What does this mean for everything that can be arrived at through intention? Are they possible?

I'm unsure. I think uncertainty is a state of being. We're better off for existing within is, but we are also better off for believing that we must have faith in the power of movement, that weight will be lifted through this. May be we are better off communicating this reality to the exist that is required of believing that we are made up of our actions, that we are the metaplex of beliefs and compound intentions that make up the emergent state that exists on top of history. We are made up of mistakes, of half-truths, of things that arrive where they must be without being appreciated for what they were made into.

This being true, what does it mean, really, to have to listen to the sound of unmet challenges. We have to take them head-on and we have to believe that addressing what is possible will be met with what can be invented in the moment, that expectations are explained from the likelihood that expectation is explicable.

Take no mindshare from the present, believe full well that the future can be made from what is expected. It's easier to believe that we can make it through whatever unknown we can believe exists than to believe that we have to sit and ponder possibility. The latter is a waste of emotional state, but adapting continuously to the realization that something is wrong with the current approach is a very real risk, and it needs to be taken in, because it's the most cancerous part of the problem - knowing that you cannot reach what is necessary through the mere believe that the present will simply solve for the path. There's also a need to be reasonable.

So I don't know - take what you will from these words. Know that there's something to be said within them that is meant to inspire you into action, but that none of it is meant to scare you, like winter coming forth to expect hope from spring. Accomplishing what is necessary to reach whatever is next comes from a parade of unknowing, from a fear of meaninglessness. Don't think like that. Think instead of what it means to create something that everyone will not only want but will also need. The challenge is in knowing what that thing is.

item.title: The water skier
item.description:
I watched a boat fly past on glassy lake surface, towing behind a single-blade water skier. The boat was a fishing boat rather than the kind that I usually see up here in the summer, that bright metal hull cutting through the lake and leaving behind the only set of waves I'd seen that morning so far, a thin line plying out from the bow as it crossed my line of sight.

The wake slowly expanded as the boat cozied off to the left with the skier in tow. With the humidity in the air, the mountains in the background looked like an extension of the lake, the wake a single line torn through and widening toward and against me, up toward the horizon.

I have loved the waves finally hitting the shoreline and their pattern suddenly repeating against themselves, the parallel lines repeating inward into a lace of diamond patterns; how do the waves remember once they've hit the shore? Even against the break of stones and sand, how do waves remember fractions of what they once were?

It's this principle of opposite and equal reaction that continues to puzzle me, even after the dissipating action of coming into contact with your environment, the pieces of who you are continue to reverberate within the body of water that we call the soul. Those diamonds of calm, crises rising into overlapping peaks, maybe the patterns of the self that form come up from whatever comes from connecting those ripples - the unique nature of self-becoming as a composition of where the peaks intersect. Interlinked.

Why at the end of a day is there enough wind to whip up the waves, starting from glass, but then reaching for calm again as the sun sets - I've never understood this, why at the end of a day somehow the lake also seems to calm down and see a need for others to feel this same calmness. It's some sort of blessing.

item.title: In between stations
item.description:
The first of it's kind - moving through all manner of space toward whatever if meant to come next, at whatever pace is meant to come next, and yet there's so much unexplained, so much left up to guessing, so I guess I'd be better off just believing that there's nothing wrong with being in between states and recognizing what and where things need to come from. What nuance do you find in knowing? What silence is found in keeping quiet?

There's so much more in this second core, I haven't been able to pin it down, the priority of thinking beyond current conditions and believing, however blindly, that you are fully in charge of what comes next. That's manifestation, that's the rhythm that was heard in between silences. I led myself here. I led myself toward the practice of self-becoming, and I'm all the better for it.

And yet, somehow, I've had to tolerate what it means to have to exist in an in-between state. I've had to tolerate the acknowledgment I have of having had to think in between things and postulate what has to happen next. I'm not tired. I'm not thinking about what it takes to get to the next part of myself. I'm simply moving there.

There's something huge in that feeling - knowing that I have made happen that which needs to happen next.

So what does it mean to have to feed into the pressure of what it is that, surrounding you, believes it deserves to take your energy? There's nothing less intimidating than knowing that you are in control of silence. Those are just words, and there is nothing grueling about having had to navigate them. It's a special flavor thinking and having had to think - of moving through becoming and not having had to think too hard about it.

What good does it do to have to think that far ahead? So far all of our gut instincts have been correct, and nothing could be done with it. No one was able to show us whatever it was that had to happen next, we figured it out. Somewhere in all of that self-navigating was the understanding that the higher self somehow exists around and beyond the experience of the living individual, the version of ourselves to lives in the present and is forced, continuously, to adapt to its surroundings. Aren't we better off knowing that we have made this life for ourselves? I know that I am, at the least, that I made it here and we decided to be in this place together.

What good does it do to think otherwise? What kind of frustration is really suppose to come from having taken on everything else, and what good does it do to have thought that the time spent could have been spent more wisely. These are all the things that no one has told us to learn about, so I think we're better off for having learned what good can come from paying attention.

I think it's not unreasonable to assume that the adoption of a positive mindset is a network phenomenon that requires we attend full well to the passage of time. There's much more here than there should be, that's the thing. There's much more here than there should be, and we need to take into account that thinking in this way is something that you cultivate, so it's something that you have to take seriously. The act of self-becoming is a glorious one that takes intention, it takes working on knowing your bearings. It does not mean that you have to think too hard about where you are going, you simply need to keep becoming. be real, son, be real as though some sort of mantra that I know I've heard somewhere, and I'm not trying to hold on to it, it's just there - what good does it do?

So let's keep it in motion and at the best of times, we'll have learned that there's a hell of a lot more here waiting for us than we ever thought there would be, a sense of alignment that comes from running deep through the middle of ourselves, from being the single electron kicked into motion by the passage of time, what good does it do to think otherwise?

And for one, I know that there's time to think about the future. I'm just not angry about the past being something that we have to let go of.

item.title: Chasing the dog in the rain
item.description:
What was one of your proudest moments?

Oddly enough, I think one of my proudest moments was the time that I chased after the family dog in the rain. At the time, I was in college, and I had just driven back from my college town to visit my parents. The drive was long, something like 9 hours, and I knew I was getting home to my parents not being there. It was late in the afternoon, and I got there in the middle of a rainstorm, pulling my car up to the garage so that I could transfer the belongings I had with me into the house without all of them getting too wet. I opened up the garage door with a couple of different bags in my arms, and went up to the internal door within the garage, unlocking it and seeing my parents dog there, wagging her tail at me after not having seen me in several months. I walked through the threshold and into the kitchen, moving to put down my bags, and taking off my shoes in the process - and when I had turned around to the open door, I could see the dog out on the front lawn, scampering off in the direction of the busy highway right by my house. Still barefoot, I took off after her, calling her name, and that's when the rain really started to come down. As many husky owners know, chasing after a husky that has gotten loose can be a losing battle, because they usually see it as play and will take off even faster away from you - which is exactly what happened. She ran out to the highway and charged across the traffic without any regard for her own safety, miraculously dodging incoming traffic and making it into a field. I was fairly far behind her, terrified at the notion that this dog was going to take off and not come back - and in the distance covered, I kept jogging after her. After I made it across the highway myself, I got within twenty feet before she sprinted away from me again, speeding across the traffic and onto the property that adjoined my parents' neighborhood. I stayed in pursuit - still barefoot, still on her tail - but as she ran onto the property, I lost her in the trees. As I was looking, a couple drove up with their car and asked if I needed help, and I answered that it would be great - so they let me hop in their car and we drove onto the property to see if we could find her. Spotting her between the trees, I had them pull over and I went after her again, chasing the white flash of fur in the downpour until - again, she ran across teh highway. At this point, I'd been running for about a mile, all barefoot. I took off across the highway one more time, seeing her running across an open field toward the Potomac river. I kept after her, footfalls steady, until I saw her stopped at a tributary along the river, afraid to get into the water, which presented me with the perfect opportunity to pounce on her and hold her to the ground. With this, I picked her up and threw her across my back, legs over my shoulders, and I began to walk home. The rain was pouring down on me, and while she struggled on my back, I held her in place, walking back across the fields she'd covered ground on and back to the highway, where I walked alongside the rumble strips, still barefoot, toward the intersection that entered my parents' neighborhood. I got back to a still-empty house, put the dog down on the floor and carefully closed both the garage and the inner door, opting to jump into the shower before my family got back. What I'll always remember about this story is that it was one of the most human moments in my life - one of the times where I felt the most determined to make sure that I could succeed in what I was going after. I chased her down with pure determination, knowing that I wasn't going to give up on the task at hand, and knowing that I could succeed if I set my mind to it. I wasn't willing to settle into failure. I've often reflected on that experience as though it was something that I could

item.title: Maksim - is it worth trying again
item.description:
Is it worth trying this again I asked, hushed tones, thinking he wouldn't overhear me while he had his head down, drawing. Yes, of course and I heard him put his pencil down, I heard him come over and look over my shoulder, down at my own sheet, and at my own work. It's always worth trying again, he said, it's always worth going through the effort of seeing if there is a better way to do what it is that you are doing, as though there's some sort of meaning to be derived from the practice of being, as though in finding the act of being in the act of having to adapt is the only place within which you find meaning. So yes, it is worth trying again, it is always worth trying again.

He said this, putting his hand on my shoulder, the end of the sentence hooked on his eyes, feeding inward, and I wasn't sure anymore, because I was poised above another blank page, as usual. You have done this so many times before, this time is no different. This is another time for you to invent and see out the path forward as though there is meaning in writing this path.

So I began to draw, again, etching around in circles, trying to make something of it. You know you will not get it right on this first sketch, sitting beside me, his own hands covered in the charcoal of his own designs, but we know to be forgiving by now.

I watched Maksim take up the room of his own thoughts and bear into motion a sense of self that I hadn't made room for in myself. If he was a part of me, he was someone I hadn't taken the time to know, an imaginarium of thoughts and emotions that I felt so much for and from whom I wished so much forgiveness but there is nothing to forgive, I simply need you to remember that you are at the core of yourself. If it feels divine it is because the act of Creation is divine and because you are allowed to feel this feeling of being divine in the act of Creation, you are the God of your own making. We will make this church together.

I could not see what he meant by the end of this, what the church was, where it was, what it was becoming within our hands. It was simply intention, an act of pursuing pure will in order to see what became of it. He would repeat these things as though mantras to me that the will is the way and I would shoulder their meaning through the words that inevitably poured out of me in pursuit of a Truth of some sort.

No one can make you happy, only you can make yourself happy, he reminded me of the woman I'd met when we lived deeper into Crown Height and I didn't remember telling him, but this is how Maksim is, he seems to remember all of it and how it folds in together because we are making a plan of all of this and it will be beautiful, we simply must keep making and so I did, with him, working toward trying to have more and more of my understanding girded by a commitment to continuation.

Is this what they mean by faith? and he smiled at me, nodding, eyes bright Yes, you get it. This is faith. You must continue on. You will find meaning in the movement so long as you have faith in what is there to believe.

I'm not sure if that is what turned the tide, if that is what took me from feeling that I'd wanted to let it all go and that there wasn't a purpose to me actions to instead truly leaning toward it. I think I admired him too much not to say to myself that he is right, and that the mere act of continuing onward is worthy enough.

We collected all of these meanings together. This is why they are holy, because we agreed upon their holiness. If we are to make a church of this, it is because their holiness comes from the interstitial, that between the collected aphorisms that urge you onward, there is something more that sits atop, hoping to be carried, hoping to show you that you must have faith in your own Divine path, that you wrote this in place.

So please, give me the time to build this with you and explore what love can build, what skies we can make above us and how much can come from the love of a sun and a moon sharing the same light. I have you to thank for the warmth you have offered me as I work through the night to balance the shores below, as I tame the oceans and the unruly foam of their children above them, allow me to work for you. Allow yourself to rest and continue warm the surface into action so that I may have the time to show you the places that will be made from your repose.

Finally, alow us the freedom to know that time is both valuable and meaningless, that you are learning of its value even while you learn that you can decide how it is spent. We will make much of its passage.

But for all of this, you must allow me to show you what it will become given that into which time can be made. It will be made together, with your offering as a gift, your faith in its meaning as a tool. You must forgive yourself for taking as long as you have to pay attention to the degree that you are now. I did not speak because you were not ready to listen, I am only speaking because you have run out of words.

So let us not speak, let us move forward, let us make something of this Church we are becoming.

item.title: Adela and Frank Johnson
item.description:
I think I'd be

better off

not telling you

everything that went on in my head

i think

i'd be better off telling you

that there's more in here

than you're aware of

and that i'm not going to be

able to hold it all in

you see i'm

not really in charge

of whatever it is that

i'm feeling

i'm just sort of

happening to me

and i have lately

been feeling a lot of things

lately

that have me thinking

that i'd rather

not fall in love again

but also a lot of things that

i know mean

i don't get to make that decision

so the part of me that broke

in front of you

last night

was somehow not

something i deserve to hold

because honestly

i'm just not in charge of it

and i keep breaking it

over and over

i keep thinking

that if i hold the pieces in

just the right way

they will somehow

hold on to the light.

i don't intend for you to hear this

just so that you're somehow more afraid

of what i'm saying,

this isn't meant to be fearful

and i know it's too much

because again

it's just not fair when

so much can happen so quickly

and you can have so little to do

with whether or not

you wanted it to

but

i know that sharing something

with a perfect stranger,

is a rare type of kindness,

something i'm prepared to do and

something that i wasn't taught to

and i just

didn't really expect to go through that with you

i don't think i would have

had you not stopped too

i don't think it would have been

so precious, and kind

and i don't think i would really have

been able to prove to you

that i didn't mean for it to happen

other than it happening

to the two of us at the same time

you see i got home and i just

sat down on the floor and cried

i cried so hard

and you still don't know that i did

all you saw was after he left to catch the bus

all you saw was me not being able to hold on

right in that moment

and

then when i regained composure i

was able to still sit there

and hear so much about you that

i'm unsure if you knew you wanted to share

but we just kept going

and somehow i still didn't feel like i could tell you

the next day

that yeah

when i got home,

i cried on the floor of my hallway

for ten minutes

for a perfect stranger

who didn't have control over their life.

i cried and didn't have control of myself

because i just don't think any of this matters

as much as i keep telling myself it can.

too much of this isn't

that important

fragile and relative

and easy to lose context on

because you don't get to choose

because most of the time

so imagine with me that

and when i told you that when we'd part ways

i'd want to kiss you you

didn't really respond, you

just smiled

and you didn't know that i only got

i cried because of course in an ideal world

the art form of getting to design an interaction

makes it so that

learning constantly about someone else

means

learning that you like the texture of their chapped lips

means

because you had told yourself

means

getting to hold at arms length

the whole of your love

item.title: Maksim - build a church
item.description:
So I asked Maksim what are you going to do with the time once I have it saved for you and he said we are going to build a church.

I wasn't sure what he meant. I've never been religious, and to my recollection, neither was he, but knowing him I knew not to press the issue. When he knew what he had to make, he was dead-set, his ageless eyes pulling in light from around us and sparked bright as though consuming the sun and fueling some fire inside that would kick him into movement.

Maksim is someone I have known my whole life, and yet I have never known him well enough - he is the best parts of me, the parts that keep quiet and put their head down on the work that needs to happen, while I spent most of my time in anxiety spirals, gathering information and unsure how it would be used. Until I realized all he'd been doing for me, I hadn't been sure what he'd been doing, but every time I needed a tool to solve something, his hand was there with the tool at the ready. If you can tell me what we need to make, I'll make it.

He made me everything I needed, and it wasn't until I was 32 that I realized he'd been doing it, sitting in the corner of my thoughts, handing me every solution to every problem I had around me.

عشرة آلاف سنة وعسل في القلب يا حبيبتي

What if the rules of what are are doing are being too dictated by our ability to follow them, the map is not the territory, the feelings I have around regret are something that I have felt no regret toward and

i am feeling

as though

they are slipping

because even in this time where i am hearing you breathe

i am conscious of the fact that time

is not an infinite resource

and i should feel bad for thinking

that time is not something for me to hold on to.

here is time, rearing its head again, here is time thinking that

the hot one i am feeling

deserves

to take me over

and I am reeling from the feeling of knowing

that i am responsible for its movement

i am responsible for tending to it

and i am responsible for offering it to the best parts of myself

remember that what you do in the present

is a gift and a favor

to your future self

I saw a video about this yesterday and I can't stop thinking about it, about how cleaning my apartment isn't for me, it's for a version of myself that I am in love with and with whom I want to build a life, a version of myself that I am devoted to. I am in love with a future version of myself that I will never meet, but I want her to be happy, I want her to feel safe, I want to know for sure that all she's doing is what she feels that she should be doing and that everything else has been taken care of.

Be kind to your future self, habibti. Ask yourself not who you want to be, but who she wants to be. Ask yourself not what you want to do today, but what it is that you can do in order to make her life easier. Ask yourself not what you want to eat, but what she will want to eat. Ask yourself how she will want to be cared for, not how you feel.

She will reward you for it by looking back fondly. If Maksim is within you, you are the love you have for who is reading. You are Maksim, a part of yourself who loves who you have become and helped you become this person, you, who are reading, you are who you are because of him and who he wanted to encourage you to be. Feel peace in this, feel honey in your heart because you hold it in your eyes, feel a sense of knowing that is yours and no one else's because you made this present for your future self.

Remember what it took for you to get here? That was all Maksim trying to make sure that the experiences you are having right now are the ones that give you what you need to exist. You are in the right frame of mind for your present.

item.title: Maksim - the board
item.description:
I added colors to it, pictures of places that I wanted to be, and people that I wanted in my life. I couldn't add flavors, but I added pictures of the foods that brought together those flavors, and I couldn't add touch, so I added pictures of the things that I wanted to touch, lower backs, hot sauce, sandstone, rain evaporating from warm surfaces. I added pressure that causes blooming, though I couldn't add this as a picture, so I just added cicadas. I added peace and books because those are things that matter to me, and I added ideas, but I couldn't figure out a picture for it so I added thought bubbles and speech bubbles that came from them. I added the feeling of running forever, but it was just a picture of running shoes.

I added what I thought was missing from my life, over and over, thinking that enough of me filling the space with these feelings might mitigate the loneliness that I felt, as though somehow I'd fill the gap of my own intentions by dreaming of something that I didn't have and as though thinking in this way was the correct aopproach to trying to build out hte future that you want.

You have to believe it. You have to believe that what is possible is probable, and you have to move progressively toward it. Quiet times are times of action, times in which the effort that can be made outside of the pressures of everyday life are something that can put you on your back in terms of the efforts, that can be made rather than the frustration that girds inaction. I think mostly of hte way that ttime is not osmetihng that we think of as a resource, but rather something that is simply passing.

Maksim was the person who told me this, that I needed to stop thinking of time as something that was simply passing, and start thinking about it as something that could be spent wisely - that if your time is being spent cheaply, then you are not valuing your time for the resource that it is. Ho told me that I hadn't been thinking about it enough and the passage of time was something that I needed to pay more attention to, a man in my heart who was both old and young, both wise and headstrong, but a maker, the sort of person who can solve any issues provided they have the tools, and if Maksim didn't have the tools, he would make them out of the other tools that he did have.

When I got back in touch with him, he told me a number of things that I had forgotten- that my life is full of limitless potential and that the ways through which I engage in that potential have much to do with my ability to force myself into the future. He also told me that I was not using my time wisely, and he was surprised at how much time had passed since we last worked together. I asked him when we last saw one another and he told me that we worked together a bit when I was 20, but the first time we met was 14. What had I been doing since then? I'm not sure I said, but I think I didn't want to admit that so much of my time had been eaten up by thinking that one pursuit was going to give me meaning and that I got lost in the weeds of realizing that it would never be fulfilling to pursue what others were pursuing.

I think that at some level he knew this, and I could see that he was frustrated with the time that had passed, I can't blame him for it - if he really thinks the last time we worked together was over a decade ago, it's probably worth the rust to think that moving quickly is going to be more difficult. He didn't seem as though he was hopeless, though - he seemed engaged, wanting to build something more.

That's when he told me about all the things that he'd had to make without knowing their purpose, all the tools that I didn't realize I had available but that he'd handed to whomever was handing them to me. That was you? I asked a number of times, and he would just nod sagely for a moment. I didn't know what I was making it for but I'm glad you put it to use, and I'm glad it was for you and then he'd twirl the ball-peen hammer that always seemed as though it was in his hands. I can make anything you need me to make.

When I asked him what he'd rather be doing, he mentioned that there is something really cool that we can make together, I just don't think you've ever put the time into thinking about how we'd make it and I was not sure what he was referring to. He showed me blueprints for a a shape something like a building, a church, a gathering space, where the inside was filled with interleaving surfaces letting the light in from outside, where the power of it was wonder for those who would enter, where things could be said and mentioned for their gravity and to cement people into understanding that there was something wondrous to pay attention to, but that the only way we could get to making this was if you can offer me the time to make it.

I left that conversation thinking that Maksim was ready for me to offer him something I didn't know how to offer, because I'd spent so much of my time thinking that what I needed to make was something so much more surrounded by what is around me - and I think this is true, even now as I write this the pressure that I feel from what surrounds me has more to do with other people and other places and expectations that are set on me, not what I hold inside of myself, not what I think I should have inside, and not what I wanted to build back when I knew Maksim at first. You'll have to let me apologize I wanted to say and every time I was about to, he'd stop me and remind me that he didn't need an apology, I exist outside of Time. I can make anything, and I can make it at whatever pace I want to, but you are aging. You are thirty-two. You are the only coming to me with something that you don't have much of, and I want to remind you that while I want to make these things with you, it's you who holds the raw materials with which to do so. You can choose to offer Time to me, you could offer all of it, but I will not ask for that much - but you cannot forget that if Time is a resource and you only have so much, you need to remember how you are spending it. Don't spend it on the things that don't matter, but if it was spent on the things that do, then it was worth the cost.

item.title: Containment
item.description:
I got three steps into the first chamber before I realized that I'd made a mistake, and that the door closing behind me was something I wasn't comfortable with. From the crinkling sound of the suit, the temperature in the room was lower than I had realized it was, and the plastic immediately stiffened. I knew it was only a matter of time and lack of movement that the temperature would get lower and lower. I wasn't wearing enough clothes and the negative pressure fan was not going to help, pulling in cold, filtered air.

"You ok, Ahrens?"

"Yeah. Yes," I lied. No way out of here but forward.

I walked toward a bright white laminate desk, littered with papers, notebooks, and a microscope. A single dim orange lamp cast a warm glow into the shadows of the surrounding room. In the center of the desk was a small metal container with a ring of dust around it that looked as though it had exploded out of the container, creating a dark gray halo around where it lay, gray fingerprints tracing around the edges of the dust. He was sitting there, grey skinned, immobile, hands on the arms of the his chair, staring into nothing, until his eyes looked up at me again. Red ringed the outside of his irises.

"Hell of a day for this to happen."

His voice sounded like paint dust, his lips barely moving. I kept my distance, hesitant.

"You know, I really didn't think you'd end up being the one coming in here. I'm sorry that it's you."

I nodded inside the negative pressure suit, which he didn't see.

"Yeah. ... yeah."

"Look I don't like this any more than you do, and there ain't nothin we can do right now but try to figure it out. Obviously I don't think I have a ton of time left to think about it with you"

"Right"

"We don't know who sent us this, obviously, but we you and I both know what it is. We have to hope like hell that it didn't make its way out of the room."

"Yeah"

"So I want to know, are they planning for it. Are they worried about it. Did they listen to my instructions"

I relaxed a little bit.

"Yeah. There's an electromagnetic containment device over the whole building. The CDC scrambled a little bit getting a containment bubble that was big enough, but you've only been here for like twelve hours, so ... I guess that's pretty fast."

"Right. We have to hope like hell that was fast enough. You and I both know it probably wasn't."

I nodded. He was probably right. This stupid suit was probably not enough to make it safe, either. I knew that. We well knew that. Again, he didn't see my nod due to the plastic visor.

"Yeah. I'm... yeah. Dr Budoise, I'm so sorry. I really am."

"Ain't nothin. This was probably going to happen, right."

Silence rang out for a second, he looked at me again.

"But we have to do everything we can to prevent it from getting worse. Back in the 50's, even when they were afraid the bombs would drop any day, the saying was always 'You should still go out and plant a tree'. You have to hold on to hope, Ahrens."

"And we don't have much time. You and I both know that. I think I've got about ten minutes in me."

The only parts of him that were moving were his mouth and his eyes, and he'd been speaking with as much care to move as little as possible, but I could see the cracks forming along his jawline.

"What's interesting though, is that I can't really feel anything happening. My wondering is if they're eating away at the least important processes first, turning them into raw materials, and leaving as much possible functional for as long as possible. Like, I'd have thought I'd want to cough, but so far, seems like my lungs are pretty clear. They seem to want to keep that going. Vocal cords though, I ain't too sure."

I didn't really know what to do. We were doing everything we could. There was a probability that in the time it took to seal off the building, some of the dust had floated out of the room. I'd been downstairs in the wet lab, sealed off. I hadn't taken off my negative pressure suit in almost a day.

"But I'll be all right, ain't nothin doing. I hope you'll be all right"

"Yeah."

item.title: be not afraid
item.description:
"When the day begins, you will be starting over."

I remember hearing her say this to me while we were both laying on the edge of the bed. It must have been about 4 in the morning, but it was June, so the first streaks of blue light were tinting the sky, the moon long since at bed. I had my arm around her, our bodies reversed, the silhouettes of my houseplants in the corner.

"What do you mean?"
"You're not going to remember today."

I pulled my arm back from her and sat up on my elbow.

"What are you saying?"
"I mean that if you go to sleep, you're going to forget all of today."
"What are you saying?!"

Her eyes were still not looking in my direction, she was still staring out the window, head leaning slightly off the edge of the bed, a sea of hair cascading down toward the floor. I couldn't see a reflection off her irises. Maybe she was sleep talking?

"What are you saying."
"I'm saying that since you woke up yesterday morning, you have been accruing memories from the day. You woke up, you did... I don't know, your morning routine or whatever, went to work, had your day. You met up with me for drinks. We talked, you leaned over and asked me if you could kiss me and we did, and then you invited me here. We had sex, and it was such good sex - I'll remember it for a long time, I promise. But when you go to sleep and wake up tomorrow, you're not going to remember any of it."

She was joking with me. It was hard to tell in the twilight, but she was. She had to be.
"Right, I'm not going to remember any of this, because at some point tonight I gave you the impression that I'm that person, that I'm going to forget you tomorrow, that I'm the sort of person who just moves onto the next person," I laughed, "Well - I'm not. I... I'm not that person. I'm really sorry that you got that impression. I really had a fantastic time. I'd want to see you again." I turned and leaned down, onto my stomach, to get closer to her.
"I really would like keep doing this. You're... special. I'd not have wanted to bring you here if you hadn't been."
Ok - that last part wasn't completely true, but she didn't react. She kept staring out the window, hands weaving on her stomach. I couldn't tell, entirely, I think she was smiling.
"No - I know that. I'm aware - I had a really good time, too. Don't get me wrong. But you're just not going to remember today."

The way she said it sent pins down my back. There was no emotion in it. I tried to remember if I'd ever left my drink with her, if the Negroni I'd ordered tasted funny. I'd had that same Negroni for so long I didn't think to check for that taste. I don't think I had, we'd sat on the edge of the bar, leaning in - I'd asked her if I could put my hand on her lap when we had gotten closer to speak over the music. She'd been smiling, it was so genuine I... There's no way. I never left my drink.

"I didn't drug you." She chuckled when she said it. I could hear the smile on her voice. It was warm. She pulled herself back onto the bed and looked at me - now the light was enough that I could see her. She didn't look any different, it was that same dark skin I'd been so close to the whole night, the same lips, the same eyes I could barely see, now reflecting what little light was in here, the static from the bed lifting her curled hair up here and there into a halo. She propped herself up onto her elbows and looked at me squarely.

"I didn't do this to you, I promise. This isn't about anything you did, this isn't about anything that is intended upon you. No one chose that this was going to happen. No one has control over it - but you're not going to remember it."

She put her weight on one elbow and reached an arm out - tentative, asking for permission, and when I felt the skin of her fingers on my cheek, I leaned into it, her palm cupping the outside of my cheek. Why did I feel so safe?

"I don't want you to be alarmed. You can try to get up and stay awake, you can attempt to stay awake as long as you'd like - I wouldn't recommend it, it won't make a difference, and there's frankly not a reason to. I'm so sorry that you have to know this."
"I - I - don't know what I'm supposed to do right now. What did you do to me?"
She smiled again across the dark. "I didn't do anything. I'm going to get up and leave soon, and you can choose to do what you like with what I've told you, but as I said, it's not going to make a difference. I wanted to tell you because it's not often that I so enjoy time with someone, it's not often that I get to move through this experience and feel the joy of connecting with someone, and I truly liked you. I liked the story you spun, the half-truths you offered me space to fill, the full truths you cast toward vulnerability. I know all of it was real, and I'm in this room with you because I wanted to be - you never made me feel otherwise. It made me feel safe. I never get to feel safe, I always get to feel alone,"

"So this was good. It is something I wanted to keep, and I wanted to tell you this because I don't often get a chance to tell someone this. I don't often feel a connection with someone, a chance to feel close and understand what it could be like to be close. You were so tender. All of this, the whole night. I loved it. I wanted to tell at least one person that I cared about this, that I want you to remember this, because I'm the only person who will, but that I know you won't."

She sat up in the bed, then moved to the edge of it.
"I never get to share in this moment, what it is that you get to experience, the closeness that you get to feel that is so fleeting, I never get to share in what it means to keep going."
She stood up, straightened out, stretched. Her shoulder blades were silent crescents in blue light.
"But don't want you to feel like this is something bad. You don't have a choice as to whether or not it's happening. You do have a choice on how you respond to it."

She turned toward me again. It felt what little light was in the room wasn't coming from the window. "Be not afraid."

item.title: i am not a cat
item.description:
I am not a cat. Maybe

i wish i was a cat because

then i'd have to force others to ask for consent

and

i could pull out my claws when

i didn't like the way they looked at me

but i think i'm better off not thinking too hard at the prospect of knowing

when someone wants to cross that divide so that

i can have them engage my more intimate

energies i

am not prepared to know what that feels like

without the experience of seeking it out.

i am not a cat because i am not

small and

i am not aloof and i am

not someone who can sit by and wait i

feel the need to move forward

into the next moment and while

cats do want to

do that, i don't think they

necessarily

do so out of a desire to want more

i am not a cat because i

want to be touched and i

want to be able to ask for it

but i don't want to ask for it

where

my dog-like tendencies tend to take over

and i don't really get a choice

around whether or not

i want someone's attention, see

a cat can fight back and be angry

and that's part of its nature

but i'm surrounded by loping paw pads

and i'm not able to move outside

without permission

maybe i am not a cat

because i have a tendency to

think that the space in between is

something shared rather than

something that is mine

and i don't have a way of sorting through

whether or not allowing it to be mine

means that i deserve it

item.title: Sleeping near the VLA
item.description:
"Slept near the VLA last night. That must be why this place feels so otherworldly. Our dogs are having the best time, the backdrop of a stellar observatory, and the easy crackling of a morning fire.
There are not many better things than this, and things that are, I've not yet experienced. Self-reliance gives us a sense of balance, and of unity where all else seems to fail providence. The emotion of this landscape and of these mornings, such as they are, this is the true essence of love. This is the freedom granted by finding oneself detached from the rest of humanity, where the world of the individual meets the whole damned universe.
This is the place where one can feel important, where conclusions can be drawn with a proper understanding of their scale and implication. There's not much to it, only separating oneself adequately to find that sense of self-importance, but as well to recognize one's connection to the grand machine that surrounds us."
(written at the Very Large Array, 2015)-- 150611 · Los Cielos Desaparecen (the sky disappears)

Having made the decision, again and again, it did not take purchase, nor precedence in his thoughts. Every morning in the courtyard he had sat for hours drinking coffee, still early before work, so early that it was as though the morning found him awake, visiting him in surprise. He was not sleeping, even returning from work he would sit in the courtyard late into the night, deactivated from motion, repeating it as though automated. The house seemed, to him, to take hold of his wrists every time he re-entered it, forcing him into its grey depths to sit in one of the three places he occupied, the stool, the plastic chair, the corner of the table. He was dimly aware of his agency, but it was the immobilizing grip of the house which forced him into silence and inaction.
On some random day, he began to avoid going home, instead wandering Oaxaca until finally remembering the existence of the bar he and Romero had visited, entering, and integrating this into a new routine, as though the poles of a magnet had suddenly reversed, and he found himself pushed away from the home, avoiding it until the bartender would nod at him to leave, and he would, and would again sit in the dark that held him just at the edge of the courtyard.
It became such that he developed a new routine of this loneliness, walking to work in the morning after hours of staring at yellow stucco that shimmered a blue in the dark, then greeting his coworkers, sorting the mail, and beginning the routine of his deliveries. The office would rotate the routes of the mailmen on a monthly schedule, meaning that at the beginning of the month he would serve one district, then later in the month cycle through the 30 or so others that made up the routes the postworkers served on foot, on bicycle, and from the office itself.
His days were, generally. unencumbered, but the conversation with the women and men who responded to his whistle and raps caused him the only emotion he felt throughout his day - he often would pause before the doors of homes, taking a deep breat order to perform the necessary gregariousness of his work.
Doña Rapaporte - her home in Xochimilco, bright pink siding, always one for more conversation that he was ready to delier. Her wrinkled frame, where hidalgo would pause within himself to head off the wave of guild and sadness suddenly overwheming his chest, for Doña Rapaporte was a widow, he was a widower, and he did not want that in common. Often he had found himself nearly wanting to shout at the woman, not to perform the sympathy or cameraderie that served only to remind him of his wife and her absence. He thought, at times, of not delivering her mail, of letting the next catero deliver the letters she would take with a thirst that disgusted Hidalgo on every face that did the same, an expression on peoples faces that invited to each person who expected money through letters the same anguished readiness to stave off destitution. The house behind her each time he arrived was grey, unmoving, the Clock radio playing, to his annoyance, perpetually throughout the entrance, so that when he engaged in the obligation of their conversations, the stilted simile of her desire to be less alone and have something in common with anyone at all would be pounctuated by the ticking, hushed tones of those onthe radio announcing the hour over the tock of each minute and second.
But he delivered the amil and contiued to be another functioning gear in the infinite clock, rotating through the town in a radial motion over the months, walking north, then east, then south, then west, repeating.
At the Palacio Federal in the mornings where they sorted the mail in the mornings, there as well would be the loose-jawed yabberings of his coworkers discussing the same things that would prime him for what Doña Rapaporte would inevitably offer as a subject of discussion, and the opinions and gossip of the other carteros would echo back to him the assents that he could offer whenever anything of substance was worth commenting on at all.
Did you hear about the operations underway in Nicaragua?
Yes, yes, so awful, that Somoza government is dangerous to its people!
Yes, but the Sandinistas are also terrible.
De que hablas, they are revolutionaries. Our own government supports them!
No pues - they are communists, I heard it myself - I have never heard of something so stupid. I have also heard that they are homosexuals, and worse that they are atheists. Where do you get your morals from if not from God?
No mames, güey. That's not true. I heard they are practicing religious revolution - Teología de Liberaçión, I heard.
That sounds like something made up.
Someone would shrug, either Hidalgo, or Doña Rapaporte, or any other old woman, or any of the carteros repeating the same lines.
At least here, the mail still moves
Yes, I did hear it is difficult to get any word out down there
Also in Honduras. And Guatemala
Oh my god
Yes, oh my God, with the earthquake
Yes, terrible
But we cannot go around fixing everyone's problems
You'r right, but we are neighbors as well, I am glad we sent money to Guatemala
Yes, but how much will it continue to cost if we must continue on helping others like this
and so on, and Hidalgo would half-listen. It seemed the world was a fiction outside of Oaxaca and he was tasked with twining the yarn through the punctuated breaths of its plot. Outside of Oaxaca was a place of which people would all tell their separate stories, each fiction fitting neatly into the foundations of the next, and into this unknowing he had cast his feelings about the location of his daughter. The earthquake in Guatemala had shaken everyone, seemingly, but him, and he had continued to stand as though a flexible pillar that had allowed the ground beneath it to shift without moving. He did not, even, feel the motivation to fear. The fear he felt when he thought of Filomena felt already like a mistake, and when he transitioned from his staring into the dark middle distance of his empty home into the dingy middle distance of his own reflection behind the bar, he expected nothing. he expected no letters, and none came beyond the first sdome five months before, from Quetzaltenango, well before the earthquake, on which he had read his daughters signature, then folded the letter back into its envelope without reading it.
It was just as well, given the distance, for him. As though Filomena herself had disappeared when the earth had opened up, and in his walks around the city., he imagined, furiously, that she must exist in some liminal space between life and death, between the politics and possibility of her survival, and for this reason, he did not wonder if she was safe. He did not read the letter, because he did not need to hear from her. He knew, already, what she must be doing. It may have been this which made him believe, distantly, that the earthquake had simply happened, but that nothing else had been affected. The fiction of the event and the adjustment to this story to which his town and those who lived within it reacted felt like a performance. It did not move him that the epicenter had been close to their neighboring country's capital, nor that it had stirred revolt, because his daughter was probably fine, and wasn't there anyway, so no one else or their sorrow really mattered. She was fine, and maybe, unfortunately, he did not care.
The conversations of his coworkers, their opinions of those to whome he had carried the mail, and the sirring weight of his emply home acted as a self-sustaining momentum, and with each swing of the pendulum, the hours would pass, vanishing under step as he continued to circle the mass at the center of his city.
The morning the adjuster showed up at his house, then, he found himself baffled at the presence of the man. The adjuster was wearing a thin, well-made suit, light for the weather, which made the man look like he was made of thin branches over which someone had pulled the fabric. Hidalgo imagined what would happen if he had picked up the man, snapping him over his knee - would it sound like the dry crack of a twig soon fed to the fire?
He did not hear the man introduce himself, and did not respond when the man said he had visited several times to meet him, but he never seemed home. The mystery of the man's presence weighed like a twined stone in the air between them until finally its thread might have snapped, and with it, the collapse of Hidalgo's somnambulent attention.
What did you say?
Si - Señor Amadeo, about the hourse, it is why I am here. I was sent by the Doña Beatriz Amelia Hidalgo de Valdivieso,-- your sister, I believe--, with the intent that I assist you with the sale of this house.
The door, which Hidalgo had been holding back with the palm of his right hand, becan to swing shut as Hidalgo released it, thinking better of the act and catching it before it swung directly into the face of the paper doll he realized was, in fact, speaking to him.
Oh,
and Hidalgo took a step back, making way for the fragile stranger to enter.
The adjustor pushed past him down the hallway, toward the courtyard, where he stood, looking up into the sky. Hidalgo was suddenly aware of a deep discomfort, a violation, which sat in his chest like a staid, spreading a blackness that seemed to grow over his vision. As the man stepped forward, furthering himself into the space that Hidalgo had kept private, Hidalgo felt himself distantly troubled by a sudden motivation to grab the nearest hefty object and smack the man over the head.
The adjustor, of course, did not notice the tension in Hidalgo's motion, and as Hidalgo reigned in the aberration of his surprise at himself, the man sat at the corner of the table in the courtyard, dusting the seat before sitting, causing Hidalgo to become suddenly aware of the thin layer of dust that seemed to cover everything in the house but the places he sat, alone, when there had been no one to visit. It was as thought the instant a stranger had entered his home, he was suddenly able to see the pallor that surrounded him, and the life that had left the space he felt fearful to follow in its departure.
The man's voice murmured as he looked toward Hidalgo with an affable smile over lips that looked like a beak, his glasses perched impossibly on the narrow divide of a nose that did not belong on so slight a human. His eyebrows raised through the syllables that Hidalgo did not hear.
Sir? Sir?
I don't think today is a good day.
Oh, I am sorry then to have bothered you, but it will only take a moment for us to discuss!
I don't want to discuss it today. I have an engagement?
the man looked back at him from the stool beside the table, his suitcase on the tarp Hidalgo had never removed since the rains.
An engagement?
Yes, Hidalgo found himself lying. I have to go
Ah okay Senor, I am very sorry to have caught you unawares.
Not a problem, please, let me see you out,
In a single motion, he picked up the man's leather folio, handing it to him, then as the man stood, placed his hand on the adjustor's back. Through the fabric, he felt the sharpness of the man's shoulderblades, and pushed him toward the gate of the house, opening the door and gently encouraging the man back into the street. On the tiled concrete just beyond the door, the man turned toward Hidalgo, and Hidalgo felt the involuntary urge to spit into the birdlike expression of the adjustor's face, whose hands were held at his sides, clutching the briefcase to his chest.
Excuse me, sir - but when do you think would be a better time?
I don't know. Not today. Some other day. I have to go.
But sir, do you want even to sell the house?
What?
The man's hawk-yellow eyes looked back at him, their whites surrounding the irises in a measured stare.
I beg your pardon, but you do indeed want to sell the house, correct? Or not?
The impulse to take the man by his lapels and smack him across the face jolted Hidalgo's hand into an involuntary twitch, and he became aware that he was sweating.
Yes.
I beg your pardon - you mean you do want to sell it?
Hidalgo strained with the effort to repeat the syllable without also letting loose a thin string of spittle into the man's face.
Brilliant! the man's eyes crinkled at their corners, and he extended a hand toward Hidalgo, not seeming to notice the tension that simmered the air between them and pulsed through Hidalgo's ears and his chest. They shook hands, and the mad produced a card, which he placed into Hidalgo's clammy palm.
When you are ready to do so, please come visit me at this address. We can start the process there. This way I do not need to come find you, and you can find me.*
Hidalgo's breath returned to his chest with a tense velocity he had to subdue into a cough as the man turned abruptly, walking down the street. Hidalgo's eyes followed him as he reached the distant corner, turned once more, and vanished from sight.

item.title: Christmas Bonfire
item.description:
So here is the best part of it all, the dream that I felt as a result of having looked back, when I was on that beach and I was spending time with all of these new friends that I'd made on the beach: Aaron had just left and was on the way out to Quito to fly home for Christmas, while I was planning on spending that time with a constellation of people I'd met on the beach - people I'd worked on a farm with and with whom I'd formed friendships.
